# Walkthrough

Every block below is real output from `tools/dte.py` on a toy project, generated by `tools/walkthrough.py`, so it is exact for this version. The project is a small service with a config loader. Owner is `ada`, the agent is `bot`.

## Day one

Scaffold the project.

```
$ dte init
created: dte.cfg, .dteignore, .dtecoverage, decisions/ (with inbox/)
next:
  1. write the core: dte new A --name <goalName> --title "<goal>" --by <owner> --made-by human   (three to six)
  2. edit dte.cfg: authority map, the layer globs, retire mode
  3. dte vendor --from <path to a DTE checkout>: copies DTE's rule text and a render of its
     decisions into vendor/dte/, ignored by the scanner; have your agent harness load PROTOCOL.md at session start
  4. dte validate, then dte coverage: those gauges are the adoption measure
```

The owner writes the core. Ring A has no parents.

```
$ dte new A --name oneSource --title "Config comes from one source of truth at startup" --by ada --made-by human --decision "All configuration is read once at startup from a single declared source." --why "Runtime config drift caused two outages last year."
created A1 "Config comes from one source of truth at startup" at decisions/A/A1.md
  cite it as dte:A1 from what it governs
```

```
$ dte new A --name laptopRunnable --title "The service stays runnable by one person on a laptop" --by ada --made-by human --decision "Everything needed to run locally is in the repo." --why "Onboarding time is the constraint, not throughput."
created A2 "The service stays runnable by one person on a laptop" at decisions/A/A2.md
  cite it as dte:A2 from what it governs
```

The agent decides at ring B, citing both core goals. Every leaf gets a camelCase name; chat says `B1 yamlFile`.

```
$ dte new B --name yamlFile --title "Config is a single YAML file, path given by CONFIG_PATH" --by bot --parents A1,A2 --decision "One YAML file. Its path is CONFIG_PATH." --why "One file satisfies A1; an environment variable keeps local runs simple (A2)."
created B1 "Config is a single YAML file, path given by CONFIG_PATH" at decisions/B/B1.md
  cite it as dte:B1 from what it governs
```

```
$ dte new B --name schemaChecked --title "Config values are validated against a schema before use" --by bot --parents A1 --decision "Loaded config is validated; the service refuses to start on a schema error." --why "A1 makes the file the only source; a bad file must fail loudly."
created B2 "Config values are validated against a schema before use" at decisions/B/B2.md
  cite it as dte:B2 from what it governs
```

Ring C: how B2 is implemented.

```
$ dte new C --name dictSchema --title "The schema lives next to the loader as a Python dict" --by bot --parents B2 --decision "schema.py holds a dict; no schema library." --why "No dependency for one dict (A2 wants a laptop-runnable repo)."
created C1 "The schema lives next to the loader as a Python dict" at decisions/C/C1.md
  cite it as dte:C1 from what it governs
```

Then the code, and citations from it.

```
$ dte cite src/config.py B1
src/config.py: inserted '# dte:B1' on line 1
```

```
$ dte cite src/schema.py C1
src/schema.py: inserted '# dte:C1' on line 1
```

```
$ dte cite src/validate.py B2
src/validate.py: inserted '# dte:B2' on line 1
```

Three gauges, one per hop. The config file is uncited. `init` already listed its own scaffold in `.dtecoverage` with the reason it needs no decision, which is what lets 100% mean something. Coverage is a report; `--check` turns it into a gate when a project wants one.

```

No citation and no spec (1):
  config.yml
```

## A spec carries a class

A spec that cites B1 and says `covers: src/*.py` makes every file it matches built to it, so a rule about a whole class reaches the class through one spec.

```
$ dte coverage
Coverage, one gauge per hop (100% is the target; B45):

  artifacts     5/5    100.0%  cite a leaf, or are built to a spec that does  (3 through a spec's covers:)
  specs         1/1    100.0%  cite the leaf they serve
  MUSTs         0/0    100.0%  enforced by a citing test (0 more labeled *Unenforced:*)

Excluded from the artifacts gauge (.dtecoverage, 2 files under 1 reason):
     2  DTE's own scaffolding; no project decision governs it
  (--excluded lists the files)
```

## An aspect folds back

The agent files a detail of B1 as its child.

```
$ dte new C --name defaultPath --title "CONFIG_PATH defaults to ./config.yml" --by bot --parents B1 --decision "When CONFIG_PATH is unset the loader reads ./config.yml." --why "B1 needs a path when none is given."
created C2 "CONFIG_PATH defaults to ./config.yml" at decisions/C/C2.md
  cite it as dte:C2 from what it governs
```

On review it is an aspect of B1, not a question B1 leaves open, so it folds back in.

```
$ dte fold C2 --by bot
folded C2 "defaultPath: CONFIG_PATH defaults to ./config.yml" into B1 yamlFile: Config is a single YAML file, path given by CONFIG_PATH (ai, unratified)
  folded into B1; file deleted, ledger line written (text in git history)
  0 citing file(s) and 0 child(ren) now point at B1; REVIEW the merged Consequences
```

## The owner ratifies

Ratified leaves become human-held: an agent can no longer retire or move them without a human's name. Ratifying drops the drafting History; git keeps it.

```
$ dte ratify B1 B2 --by ada
ratified B1 "yamlFile: Config is a single YAML file, path given by CONFIG_PATH" by ada
  it is now human-held (B11); the owner may reword it in their own voice
  dropped ## History (B62); git keeps what was dropped
ratified B2 "schemaChecked: Config values are validated against a schema before use" by ada
  it is now human-held (B11); the owner may reword it in their own voice
```

## A subagent is briefed

An orchestrator at ring B spawns a subagent to work under B2 and hands it this block.

```
$ dte brief C --under B2
DTE BRIEF: you operate at ring C of this project's decision tree.

Rules:
  1. Decide only at ring C or deeper. Create decisions with
     `python dte.py new C --name <camelCase> --title "..." --by <you> --parents <ids> --decision "..." --why "..."`.
     A leaf is a call a person could make in plain words; a sentence that would still be true had the
     opposite been chosen is mechanics and goes in the spec (B47). A child decides a question its parent
     leaves open; one that only details its parent folds back into it (B48).
  2. Anything that belongs at ring B or shallower, or whose ring is unclear, is not yours:
     write decisions/inbox/<slug>.md and ask orchestrator.
  3. Cite what your work serves: `python dte.py cite <file> <ID>`. Refer to every decision as ID plus its name.
  4. Never change a decision made or ratified by a human. If your environment refuses an edit to the tree,
     stop and ask for an authorization that names the leaves; never route around the refusal (B53).
     Before you finish, run `DTE_RING=C python dte.py validate`; it must print OK.
  5. Before acting under a leaf marked unratified and not contested, run `python dte.py contest <ID>`
     and follow it: build the alternatives, scope their cost, judge by the parents, record the verdict.
     A contested or ratified leaf is settled: act on it and never re-ask (A7, B60).
     A leaf marked imported was re-homed, not decided; its contest is owed before the first new work under it.

Decisions above your ring that bind you relevant to B2 (2):
  ring A:
    A1 oneSource: Config comes from one source of truth at startup [human-held]
  ring B:
    B2 schemaChecked: Config values are validated against a schema before use (ai) [human-held]

Your subtree: `python dte.py tree --under B2`; read any leaf with `python dte.py show <ID>`.
```

## Reverting a decision

The agent tries to revert the human-held B2 and is refused.

```
$ dte retire B2 --by bot
B2 is human-held; retiring it needs --authorized-by <human>  (B11)
```

With the owner's authorization the revert goes through. The report is the blast radius.

```
$ dte retire B2 --by bot --authorized-by ada
retired B2 "schemaChecked: Config values are validated against a schema before use"
  reverted; file deleted, ledger line written (text in git history)
  these now fail validation until re-pointed or retired (blast radius of the revert):
    src/validate.py
    C1 dictSchema: The schema lives next to the loader as a Python dict (ai, unratified)
```

Validation now fails until every item in that radius is dealt with. C1 is an orphan; validate.py cites a retired leaf.

```
$ dte validate
ERROR   C1: ORPHAN, parent B2 was retired on 2026-10-31 (reverted); text: git log --all -- decisions/B/B2.md; re-parent, supersede, or revert C1
ERROR   src/validate.py:1: cites B2, which was retired on 2026-10-31 (reverted); text: git log --all -- decisions/B/B2.md

Unratified AI/joint decisions: 1 (0 contested, 0 imported); list: dte unratified  dte:B59, dte:B60

4 leaves, 0 pending, 5 citations in 5/7 artifacts, 2 errors, 0 warnings
FAILED
```

The agent re-parents the orphan. Frontmatter is never hand-edited.

```
$ dte reparent C1 --parents B1 --by bot
re-parented C1 "dictSchema: The schema lives next to the loader as a Python dict": [B2] -> [B1]
```

After re-pointing the citation in validate.py, the tree is consistent again. B2 lives in the ledger and in git history.

```
$ dte validate
WARNING leaves changed with no ring declared; an agent runs validate --as <its ring> (or sets DTE_RING); the owner sets DTE_OWNER=1 to silence this

Unratified AI/joint decisions: 1 (0 contested, 0 imported); list: dte unratified  dte:B59, dte:B60

Leaves changed in this working tree (report these, ID plus name):  dte:B17
  C1 dictSchema: The schema lives next to the loader as a Python dict (ai, unratified)

1 scope findings (advisory): run dte scope

4 leaves, 0 pending, 5 citations in 5/7 artifacts, 0 errors, 1 warnings
OK
```

```
$ dte retired
B2    2026-10-31  reverted           by bot  authorized by ada  "schemaChecked: Config values are validated against a schema before use"
C2    2026-10-31  folded -> B1       by bot  "defaultPath: CONFIG_PATH defaults to ./config.yml"
```

## Promoting a decision

Advisory checks. On a tree this small B1 already reads as broad; the thresholds in `dte.cfg` are guesses until calibrated on a real tree, which is why scope never fails.

```
$ dte scope
BROAD (1):
  B1 yamlFile: Config is a single YAML file, path given by CONFIG_PATH (ai)
    1 descendants (50% of non-core) and 5 implementing files (71% of artifacts); promote it, or split it into several decisions

1 findings. Advisory: thresholds and docs globs are in dte.cfg.
```

The agent decides the schema location is really a rule, not an implementation detail, and promotes it. New ID, old one retired, references rewritten.

## Integrating

The JSON is the join surface for a structural graph: `citations[].file` is the key.

```
$ dte export --out tree.json
wrote ./tree.json: 4 leaves, 5 citations, 3 retired, 0 inbox
```

That is the whole life cycle: write the core, decide beneath it, cite, cover a class with a spec, fold an aspect back, validate, ratify, brief, revert, repair, promote, export. Nothing above was typed into a frontmatter block by hand.
